calls.reason: OpenAI shipped Operator only as a research preview it said was not yet reliable, and scored 38.1% on OSWorld. The Decoder found it needed constant supervision. 'Barely works' is hyperbole, but the main point holds.
The evidence is mixed. Census data show under 8% of firms using AI, but the NBER survey found 28% of workers using generative AI at work. No data isolate use of enterprise-bought features.

The packet has only Sutskever's testimony and reports of disappointing training runs, plus an earlier small-scale paper showing predictable scaling. There are no frontier measurements of diminishing returns.
The Nature paper shows hallucination persists, and conformal-prediction work shows partial gains. Neither shows a general fix or that new mathematics is needed. No deadline is given.
Google reported over 650 million Gemini app monthly users in October 2025, well past the 500 million target he called unrealistic and before the end-2025 deadline.
The 38.1% OSWorld score and five failed MIT tests show real unreliability. But 58.1% on the harder WebArena cuts against 'only simple tasks', and no Anthropic test from the period is in the packet.
